ksparing1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: What does aldosterone do inside a collecting-duct cell?
opts: Increases the number of sodium channels
Correct. After binding its receptor and reaching the nucleus, aldosterone drives protein synthesis that adds sodium channels.
Decreases the number of sodium channels
Aldosterone increases sodium channels; lowering them is closer to the effect of the drugs that block aldosterone.
Closes the water channels
Water channels are controlled by antidiuretic hormone, not aldosterone.
Blocks potassium secretion
Aldosterone promotes sodium reabsorption with potassium loss, so it increases potassium secretion.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 34

ksparing1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: What happens to the diuretic effect of a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor after several days of use?
opts: It diminishes
Correct. The sodium and potassium loss is short-lived and the effect falls after three to five days of use.
It becomes stronger
The effect wanes rather than builds, so these are weak diuretics.
It stays unchanged
The effect does not stay constant; it is reduced over the first days of treatment.
It reverses to sodium retention
The effect shrinks over the first days but does not reverse into sodium retention.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 39

ksparing1.io: Identify indications for commonly used diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: How are potassium-sparing diuretics most often used?
opts: Alone for acute pulmonary edema
Acute pulmonary edema needs a potent loop diuretic; these drugs are too weak to be used alone.
Alone to prevent mountain sickness
Mountain sickness is prevented with a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor, not a potassium-sparing diuretic.
Alone for hypercalcemia with saline
Hypercalcemia is treated with a loop diuretic and saline; potassium-sparing diuretics are not used alone this way.
With other diuretics or antihypertensives
Correct. Their weak effect makes them most useful in combination, where they hold on to potassium that the partner drug wastes.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 32

ksparing1.io: Identify diuretics and heart failure drug classes and commonly prescribed diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: Which drug is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor?
opts: Amiloride
Amiloride is a potassium-sparing diuretic that blocks luminal sodium channels.
Acetazolamide
Correct. Acetazolamide, dichlorphenamide and methazolamide are the carbonic anhydrase inhibitors.
Eplerenone
Eplerenone is an aldosterone antagonist that acts on the steroid receptor, not on carbonic anhydrase.
Torsemide
Torsemide is a loop diuretic that inhibits the sodium-potassium-chloride carrier.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 40

ksparing1.io: Identify indications for commonly used diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: A climber ascending rapidly wants a drug to prevent mountain sickness. Which diuretic is used?
opts: Acetazolamide
Correct. Mountain sickness is a listed use for carbonic anhydrase inhibitors such as acetazolamide.
Furosemide
Furosemide is a loop diuretic used for edema and does not prevent mountain sickness.
Spironolactone
Spironolactone is an aldosterone antagonist for aldosterone-driven conditions, not mountain sickness.
Hydrochlorothiazide
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide for hypertension and calcium stones, not altitude illness.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 42

ksparing1.io: Discuss potential drug-drug, drug-food, and drug-herb interactions with diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: A patient taking amiloride is also prescribed an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor. What is the main concern?
opts: A dangerous fall in potassium
Neither drug wastes potassium; amiloride holds it and the inhibitor also raises it, so the risk is a rise.
Loss of hearing
Hearing loss is a risk of loop diuretics, especially with aminoglycosides, and is unrelated to this combination.
A dangerous rise in potassium
Correct. Both drugs raise serum potassium, so caution is needed with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers.
Blood clots
Clotting problems are not a listed concern; the listed caution is hyperkalemia.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 33

ksparing1.io: Identify indications for commonly used diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: Aldosterone antagonists work best in which circumstance?
opts: When aldosterone levels are high
Correct. These drugs are most effective when circulating aldosterone is high, because they compete for the receptor.
When aldosterone levels are low
With little aldosterone there is little to antagonize, so the effect is smallest.
When serum potassium is low
Potassium level is not the condition that determines their effect; the amount of aldosterone is.
When urine flow is already high
Urine flow does not determine the effect; they work best when aldosterone is high.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 36

ksparing1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: Besides adding sodium channels, which other action does aldosterone have in a collecting-duct cell?
opts: Lowers sodium-potassium pump activity
Aldosterone raises pump activity, which helps move sodium out toward the blood and potassium into the cell.
Raises sodium-potassium pump activity
Correct. Aldosterone also raises the activity of the sodium-potassium pump on the blood side of the cell.
Opens the water channels
Water channels are controlled by antidiuretic hormone, not aldosterone, which adds sodium channels and raises pump activity.
Stops protein synthesis
Aldosterone works by activating protein synthesis in the nucleus, which creates new channels and pumps.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 34

ksparing1.io: Outline appropriate patient education for diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: A patient taking triamterene asks about starting a potassium supplement. What is the best advice?
opts: Take it daily to prevent weakness
Weakness from low potassium is a loop and thiazide problem; this drug raises potassium, so a supplement adds risk.
Take it only with meals
Timing with meals does not remove the risk; the problem is the total potassium load with a potassium-sparing drug.
Double the dose of triamterene
Doubling the dose would raise potassium further and does not address the question of supplements.
Avoid it unless told otherwise
Correct. Triamterene already holds on to potassium, so a supplement can push potassium dangerously high and needs caution.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 33

ksparing1.io: Identify indications for commonly used diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: Which kidney disease with edema is an indication for an aldosterone antagonist?
opts: Acute tubular necrosis
This is not a listed indication; the listed kidney condition is nephrotic syndrome.
Kidney stones
Calcium stones are a thiazide indication, because thiazides lower urinary calcium; they are not an aldosterone antagonist use.
Nephrotic syndrome
Correct. Nephrotic syndrome is one of the edematous conditions listed as an indication for aldosterone antagonists.
Polycystic kidney disease
This is not a listed indication for aldosterone antagonists; nephrotic syndrome is.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 37

ksparing1.io: Identify indications for commonly used diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: How does the diuretic effect of potassium-sparing diuretics compare with loop and thiazide diuretics?
opts: About the same as thiazides
Thiazides move more sodium than potassium-sparing drugs do, which block only a small share of sodium reabsorption.
Stronger than thiazides
Thiazides inhibit up to about 5 percent of filtered sodium chloride, more than these drugs, so they are not stronger.
Much weaker
Correct. Potassium-sparing diuretics have much less natriuretic and diuretic effect than loops or thiazides.
Stronger than loops
Loop diuretics are the most potent class; potassium-sparing diuretics are far weaker.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 32

ksparing1.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: Which potassium-sparing diuretic is associated with megaloblastic anemia?
opts: Triamterene
Correct. Megaloblastic anemia is the reaction named for triamterene.
Amiloride
Amiloride's named reaction is azotemia; megaloblastic anemia is the one tied to triamterene.
Spironolactone
Spironolactone's distinctive effects are on sex hormones, such as gynecomastia, not on red blood cell formation.
Eplerenone
Eplerenone is notable for less androgen-receptor effect; it is not the agent tied to megaloblastic anemia.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 33

ksparing1.io: Outline appropriate patient education for diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: A woman starting spironolactone should be told to report which problem?
opts: Ringing in the ears
Ototoxicity belongs to loop diuretics, not to spironolactone.
Irregular menstrual periods
Correct. Menstrual irregularities are a recognized sex-hormone effect of spironolactone and are worth reporting.
Sensitivity to sunlight
Photosensitivity is an adverse effect of thiazides and loops, not of spironolactone.
Yellow-green halos
Yellow-green halos are a visual sign of digoxin toxicity, not a spironolactone effect.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 38

ksparing1.io: Identify diuretics and heart failure drug classes and commonly prescribed diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: Where on the nephron do carbonic anhydrase inhibitors act?
opts: Thick ascending limb
That is the loop diuretic site, not where carbonic anhydrase inhibitors work.
Distal convoluted tubule
That is the thiazide site, not where carbonic anhydrase inhibitors work.
Proximal tubule
Correct. Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors act in the proximal tubule, where bicarbonate is reabsorbed.
Collecting duct
That is the site of the potassium-sparing diuretics and aldosterone antagonists.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 41

ksparing1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: Why do amiloride and triamterene reduce urinary potassium loss?
opts: Potassium reabsorption in the loop rises
These drugs do not act in the loop of Henle; their effect is on potassium secretion in the collecting duct.
They stimulate aldosterone release
More aldosterone would add sodium channels and increase potassium loss, the opposite of what these drugs do.
The gradient for potassium secretion falls
Correct. Less sodium enters the collecting-duct cell, so the gradient that drives potassium secretion into the urine is smaller.
They block potassium filtration
Potassium is filtered freely at the glomerulus; these drugs act later by reducing its secretion in the collecting duct.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 30

ksparing1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: Which hormone controls the water channels of the collecting duct?
opts: Aldosterone
Aldosterone adds sodium channels and raises pump activity; it does not control the water channels.
Atrial natriuretic peptide
Atrial natriuretic peptide promotes sodium loss and is not the hormone that opens collecting-duct water channels.
Renin
Renin is an enzyme that starts the angiotensin cascade; it does not control collecting-duct water channels.
Antidiuretic hormone
Correct. Antidiuretic hormone acts on its receptor to bring water channel molecules into the luminal membrane.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 34

ksparing1.io: Outline appropriate patient education for diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: A patient taking acetazolamide reports unusual sleepiness. Which listed adverse effect does this match?
opts: Insomnia
Insomnia is the opposite symptom and is not a listed effect of these drugs.
Euphoria
Euphoria is not a listed adverse effect; the listed central effect is drowsiness.
Seizures
These drugs are used to treat epilepsy rather than cause seizures, and drowsiness is the listed effect.
Drowsiness
Correct. Drowsiness is a listed central nervous system adverse effect of carbonic anhydrase inhibitors.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 43

ksparing1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: Which laboratory value is most important to monitor in a patient taking an aldosterone antagonist?
opts: Serum calcium
Calcium is the value followed with thiazides and loop diuretics; the dangerous change with aldosterone antagonists is in potassium.
Serum potassium
Correct. Hyperkalemia is the main adverse effect, so potassium is the value to follow.
Serum uric acid
Uric acid rises with loops and thiazides; aldosterone antagonists have only modest effects on it.
Blood glucose
Glucose is raised by loops and thiazides; aldosterone antagonists have only modest effects on it.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 38

ksparing1.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: Compared with loops and thiazides, how do aldosterone antagonists affect lipid, glucose and uric acid levels?
opts: Only modest effects
Correct. Aldosterone antagonists have only modest effects on lipid, glucose and uric acid levels.
Marked hyperglycemia
Marked glucose rises are not a feature; thiazides and loops are the ones that raise glucose.
Marked hyperuricemia and gout
Raising uric acid to cause gout is typical of loops and thiazides, not aldosterone antagonists.
Marked hyperlipidemia
Rises in lipids are a thiazide and loop effect; aldosterone antagonists have only modest effects.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 36

ksparing1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: How do aldosterone antagonists act at the steroid receptor?
opts: Block luminal sodium channels
Blocking luminal sodium channels is how amiloride and triamterene work, not the aldosterone antagonists.
Bind it without reaching the nucleus
Correct. The antagonist binds the steroid receptor but does not translocate to the nucleus, so the aldosterone message is not delivered.
Inhibit carbonic anhydrase
Carbonic anhydrase inhibition belongs to acetazolamide and its relatives, which act in the proximal tubule.
Raise aldosterone release
These drugs oppose aldosterone; raising its release would add sodium channels and potassium loss.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 36

ksparing1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: Which combination carries the greatest risk of hyperkalemia?
opts: Furosemide with hydrochlorothiazide
Both waste potassium, so the risk is hypokalemia, not hyperkalemia.
Spironolactone with lisinopril
Correct. Lisinopril is an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor; both drugs raise serum potassium, so together the risk of hyperkalemia is high and potassium must be monitored.
Acetazolamide with furosemide
Both deplete potassium, so the risk is a low potassium level.
Bumetanide with metolazone
A loop with a thiazide-type drug wastes potassium, so hypokalemia is the concern.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 33

ksparing1.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing1.q: A patient on a loop diuretic has a low potassium. Which drug is added to offset the potassium loss?
opts: Hydrochlorothiazide
Hydrochlorothiazide also increases potassium excretion, so it would worsen the low potassium.
Acetazolamide
Acetazolamide causes potassium depletion, so it would worsen the low potassium.
Bumetanide
Bumetanide is another loop diuretic that increases potassium excretion.
Spironolactone
Correct. Aldosterone antagonists reduce potassium loss, so they can be combined with a loop diuretic.
ksparing1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 36

ksparing2.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which electrolyte disturbance sets potassium-sparing diuretics apart from other diuretic classes?
opts: Hypokalemia
Hypokalemia is the usual result of loops and thiazides; potassium-sparing diuretics do the reverse.
Hypomagnesemia
Magnesium loss is typical of loops and thiazides; the distinguishing problem of potassium-sparing drugs is a high potassium.
Hyperkalemia
Correct. The potassium-sparing diuretics raise serum potassium, the major difference from loops and thiazides.
Hypocalcemia
Calcium loss is typical of loop diuretics; the distinguishing problem of potassium-sparing drugs is a high potassium.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 33

ksparing2.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which potassium-sparing diuretic is associated with azotemia?
opts: Triamterene
Triamterene's named reaction is megaloblastic anemia; azotemia is the one tied to amiloride.
Acetazolamide
Acetazolamide is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor, not a potassium-sparing drug; its adverse effects are acidosis and potassium depletion.
Eplerenone
Eplerenone's notable feature is less androgen-receptor effect; azotemia is the reaction named for amiloride.
Amiloride
Correct. Azotemia, a rise in blood urea nitrogen, is the reaction named for amiloride.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 33

ksparing2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: What is the mechanism of action of amiloride and triamterene?
opts: Inhibit the sodium-potassium-chloride carrier
That carrier is the target of loop diuretics in the thick ascending limb, not of the potassium-sparing diuretics.
Inhibit the sodium-chloride transporter
That transporter in the distal convoluted tubule is the target of thiazide diuretics, which waste potassium.
Block luminal sodium channels
Correct. Blocking luminal sodium channels in the collecting duct cuts sodium reabsorption and reduces the gradient that drives potassium secretion.
Inhibit carbonic anhydrase
Carbonic anhydrase inhibition in the proximal tubule defines acetazolamide and its relatives, not amiloride or triamterene.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 30

ksparing2.io: Identify diuretics and heart failure drug classes and commonly prescribed diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which pair of agents are the aldosterone antagonists?
opts: Amiloride and triamterene
These block luminal sodium channels directly; they do not act on the aldosterone receptor.
Spironolactone and eplerenone
Correct. Spironolactone and eplerenone are the aldosterone antagonists.
Acetazolamide and dichlorphenamide
These are carbonic anhydrase inhibitors that act on the proximal tubule.
Metolazone and indapamide
These are thiazide-type diuretics acting on the distal convoluted tubule, not aldosterone antagonists.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 35

ksparing2.io: Identify diuretics and heart failure drug classes and commonly prescribed diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Triamterene is commonly combined in one product with which diuretic?
opts: Furosemide
Furosemide is a loop diuretic; the potassium-sparing combination products pair with hydrochlorothiazide instead.
Hydrochlorothiazide
Correct. Triamterene (and amiloride) are marketed in combination with hydrochlorothiazide, whose potassium loss the partner offsets.
Spironolactone
Spironolactone is another potassium-sparing drug; combining two would add hyperkalemia risk rather than offset a loss.
Acetazolamide
Acetazolamide depletes potassium and causes acidosis; the combination products use hydrochlorothiazide.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 31

ksparing2.io: Identify indications for commonly used diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which neurological disorder is an indication for carbonic anhydrase inhibitors?
opts: Epilepsy
Correct. The metabolic acidosis and central nervous system effects of these drugs make epilepsy an indication.
Parkinson disease
Parkinson disease is treated with dopaminergic therapy, not carbonic anhydrase inhibitors.
Multiple sclerosis
Multiple sclerosis is treated with disease-modifying immunotherapy, not carbonic anhydrase inhibitors.
Meningitis
Meningitis is treated with antimicrobial therapy and is not an indication for these drugs.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 42

ksparing2.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which acid-base disturbance do carbonic anhydrase inhibitors cause?
opts: Metabolic alkalosis
Contraction alkalosis is the typical result of loops and thiazides; carbonic anhydrase inhibitors do the reverse.
Respiratory acidosis
The primary disturbance is metabolic, from bicarbonate loss, not a failure to breathe off carbon dioxide.
Respiratory alkalosis
Overbreathing may follow, but the disturbance these drugs cause is a metabolic acidosis.
Metabolic acidosis
Correct. Loss of bicarbonate in the urine causes a metabolic acidosis, unlike the contraction alkalosis of other diuretics.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 43

ksparing2.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which adverse effect in men is characteristic of spironolactone?
opts: Gout
Gout from raised uric acid is a loop and thiazide effect; spironolactone has only modest effects on uric acid.
Gynecomastia
Correct. Gynecomastia, or breast enlargement in men, is the characteristic sex-hormone effect of spironolactone, which blocks the androgen receptor.
Megaloblastic anemia
Megaloblastic anemia is the reaction named for triamterene, a different potassium-sparing drug.
Hearing loss
Hearing loss is a loop diuretic effect, not a spironolactone effect.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 38

ksparing2.io: Identify indications for commonly used diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which condition is an indication for an aldosterone antagonist?
opts: Primary aldosteronism
Correct. Primary aldosteronism, an excess of aldosterone, is a direct indication for these drugs.
Acute pulmonary edema
Acute pulmonary edema calls for a potent loop diuretic; aldosterone antagonists are weak diuretics.
Mountain sickness
Mountain sickness is treated with a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor such as acetazolamide.
Calcium oxalate kidney stones
Calcium stones are a thiazide indication, because thiazides lower urinary calcium.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 37

ksparing2.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: A man taking spironolactone develops breast enlargement. Which change in therapy is appropriate?
opts: Switch to eplerenone
Correct. Eplerenone has less effect on androgen receptors, so it causes less gynecomastia.
Add a thiazide diuretic
A thiazide does nothing for the breast enlargement and adds potassium loss and other adverse effects.
Switch to acetazolamide
Acetazolamide is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor with a different action and acidosis as its problem; it does not replace an aldosterone antagonist.
Add a potassium supplement
Spironolactone already holds potassium, so a supplement raises the risk of hyperkalemia and does not help the breast changes.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 38

ksparing2.io: Identify indications for commonly used diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which agents are carbonic anhydrase inhibitors applied to the eye for glaucoma?
opts: Timolol and betaxolol
These are beta blockers used in glaucoma, with a different mechanism.
Latanoprost and bimatoprost
These are prostaglandin analogs that increase aqueous outflow.
Dorzolamide and brinzolamide
Correct. Dorzolamide and brinzolamide are the topical carbonic anhydrase inhibitors for glaucoma.
Pilocarpine and carbachol
These are cholinergic agonists used in glaucoma, not carbonic anhydrase inhibitors.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 42

ksparing2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which two hormones control the collecting duct?
opts: Renin and angiotensin II
These act upstream in the renin-angiotensin system; the hormones that act directly on the collecting duct are aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone.
Aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone
Correct. These are the two hormones that act on the collecting duct, which is why it is the site of the potassium-sparing diuretics.
Insulin and glucagon
These regulate glucose, not collecting-duct handling of sodium, potassium and water.
Parathyroid hormone and calcitonin
Parathyroid hormone acts at the distal convoluted tubule on calcium; the collecting duct is controlled by aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 11

ksparing2.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which diuretic classes deplete potassium?
opts: Loops, thiazides and aldosterone antagonists
Aldosterone antagonists hold on to potassium rather than depleting it.
Amiloride, triamterene and spironolactone
These three spare potassium and can cause hyperkalemia rather than depleting it.
Loops, thiazides and carbonic anhydrase inhibitors
Correct. These three classes increase potassium excretion or deplete it.
Eplerenone and carbonic anhydrase inhibitors
Eplerenone spares potassium and does not deplete it, so the pairing is wrong.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 43

ksparing2.io: Identify diuretics and heart failure drug classes and commonly prescribed diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which part of the nephron is the site of action of the potassium-sparing diuretics?
opts: Proximal tubule
The proximal tubule is where carbonic anhydrase inhibitors act, and most filtered bicarbonate, glucose and amino acids are reclaimed.
Collecting duct
Correct. The collecting duct, where aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone act, is the site of the potassium-sparing diuretics.
Thick ascending limb
The thick ascending limb is the loop diuretic site, where the sodium-potassium-chloride carrier works.
Distal convoluted tubule
The distal convoluted tubule is the thiazide site; the potassium-sparing drugs work further along, in the collecting duct.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 11

ksparing2.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which acid-base and potassium changes are the main adverse effects of aldosterone antagonists?
opts: Hypokalemia and alkalosis
These are the effects of loops and thiazides; aldosterone antagonists spare potassium and cause mild acidosis.
Hyperkalemia and alkalosis
Hyperkalemia is right, but the acid-base change is a mild acidosis, not an alkalosis.
Hypokalemia and acidosis
Aldosterone antagonists raise potassium; the low potassium paired with acidosis fits carbonic anhydrase inhibitors.
Hyperkalemia and mild acidosis
Correct. Holding on to potassium causes hyperkalemia, along with a mild metabolic acidosis.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 38

ksparing2.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which laboratory abnormalities should be watched in a patient taking acetazolamide?
opts: High bicarbonate and high potassium
This reverses both findings; these drugs lower bicarbonate and deplete potassium.
Low bicarbonate and high potassium
Bicarbonate falls, but carbonic anhydrase inhibitors deplete potassium rather than raising it.
Low bicarbonate and low potassium
Correct. Metabolic acidosis lowers bicarbonate, and potassium depletion lowers potassium.
High bicarbonate and low potassium
Potassium falls, but these drugs cause an acidosis with low bicarbonate, not an alkalosis.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 43

ksparing2.io: Identify indications for commonly used diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors lower pressure in which eye disease?
opts: Cataract
A cataract is a clouded lens and is not treated with carbonic anhydrase inhibitors.
Conjunctivitis
Conjunctivitis is infection or allergy of the conjunctiva and does not call for these drugs.
Dry eye
Dry eye is treated by restoring tears and lubrication, not by carbonic anhydrase inhibitors.
Glaucoma
Correct. Reducing bicarbonate in the ciliary body lowers aqueous humor production, which treats glaucoma.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 42

ksparing2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which process is reduced by carbonic anhydrase inhibitors?
opts: Bicarbonate reabsorption
Correct. Blocking carbonic anhydrase reduces bicarbonate reabsorption, along with hydrogen ion production and sodium-hydrogen exchange.
Glucose reabsorption
Glucose reabsorption is reduced by the sodium-glucose transporter inhibitors, not by carbonic anhydrase inhibitors.
Chloride secretion
Chloride secretion is not the process blocked; the main effect is on bicarbonate reabsorption.
Calcium reabsorption
Calcium handling is changed by loops and thiazides; carbonic anhydrase inhibitors act on bicarbonate.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 39

ksparing2.io: Identify indications for commonly used diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which condition raises aldosterone secondarily and is treated with an aldosterone antagonist?
opts: Cirrhosis of the liver
Correct. Cirrhosis causes secondary hyperaldosteronism, and aldosterone antagonists are used for the resulting edema.
Hypercalcemia
Hypercalcemia is treated with a loop diuretic and saline; it is not an aldosterone-driven condition.
Mountain sickness
Mountain sickness is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor indication and is not driven by aldosterone.
Glaucoma
Glaucoma is treated by lowering aqueous humor, for example with carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, not aldosterone antagonists.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 37

ksparing2.io: Identify indications for commonly used diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Besides edema, which cardiovascular conditions are indications for aldosterone antagonists?
opts: Hypertension and heart failure
Correct. Aldosterone antagonists are used for hypertension and for heart failure, along with edematous conditions.
Stable angina and arrhythmia
These are not listed indications; the cardiovascular uses are hypertension and heart failure.
Hyperlipidemia and claudication
These are not indications for aldosterone antagonists, which are diuretics and antihypertensives.
Variant angina and stroke
These are not listed indications; the cardiovascular uses are hypertension and heart failure.
ksparing2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 37

ksparing2.io: Identify diuretics and heart failure drug classes and commonly prescribed diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which pair of agents are the potassium-sparing diuretics that block luminal sodium channels?
opts: Spironolactone and eplerenone
These two are also potassium sparing, but they block the aldosterone receptor instead of the sodium channel itself.
Acetazolamide and methazolamide
These inhibit carbonic anhydrase in the proximal tubule and deplete potassium; they do not block collecting-duct sodium channels.
Furosemide and bumetanide
These loop diuretics inhibit the sodium-potassium-chloride carrier and waste potassium, so they are the opposite of potassium sparing.
Amiloride and triamterene
Correct. Amiloride and triamterene block sodium channels on the luminal side of the collecting duct, which holds potassium back.

ksparing2.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
ksparing2.q: Which gastrointestinal symptoms are listed as adverse effects of aldosterone antagonists?
opts: Constipation and bleeding
Constipation is a thiazide effect and bleeding is not a listed effect of aldosterone antagonists.
Nausea and vomiting
Correct. Nausea, vomiting and general gastrointestinal upset are listed for aldosterone antagonists.
Dysphagia and drooling
These are not recognized adverse effects of aldosterone antagonists; the gastrointestinal effects are nausea, vomiting and upset.
Jaundice and pancreatitis
These are not the typical effects of aldosterone antagonists; the gastrointestinal effects are nausea, vomiting and upset.
